findings.title: BSD-only sed -i '' breaks the script on Linux
findings.body: The line `sed -i '' -E "s|^GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=.*|GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=$TUNNEL_URL|" "$ENV_FILE"` uses BSD/macOS sed syntax. On GNU/Linux, the empty string after `-i` is interpreted as the name of the file to edit in-place, so the script will not actually rewrite `$ENV_FILE` (and may create a literal file called `''`). Use a portable form such as `sed -i.bak -E ... && rm "${ENV_FILE}.bak"` or do the substitution with another tool. This script is checked in for the whole repo and any Linux user running it for local Google Calendar webhook testing will hit the bug.

findings.title: Cache last-updated timestamp is formatted with a hardcoded en-US locale
findings.body: The component builds the cache timestamp with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { dateStyle: "short", timeStyle: "short" })`. The whole rest of the component goes through `useLocale()` and `t(...)`, but the date is forced into US format regardless of the user's locale (e.g. a French user still sees `12/04/25, 3:00 PM`). It should use the locale returned by `useLocale()` (e.g. `new Intl.DateTimeFormat(locale, { dateStyle: "short", timeStyle: "short" })`) so the displayed timestamp respects the user's preference.

findings.title: Successful cache deletion does not invalidate connectedCalendars, so UI keeps showing stale cache status
findings.body: The `deleteCacheMutation.onSuccess` only fires `showToast(...)` and calls `onSuccess?.()`. It never invalidates `trpc.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`, which is the query that supplies `cacheUpdatedAt` in `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper`. Compare with `disconnectMutation`, which does `await utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` in `onSettled`. As a result, after the user confirms "Delete cached data" the dropdown continues to render the "Cache Status" block with the old timestamp and a "Delete cached data" action until the page is refetched by some other means. Either invalidate the query here directly, or require callers to do it via `onSuccess` (and document that).

findings.title: Empty actions wrapper div is always rendered even when CredentialActionsDropdown returns null
findings.body:
The previous code only rendered the action area when `!connectedCalendar.delegationCredentialId && !disableConnectionModification`. The new code unconditionally renders `
` for both the AppListCard and the error Alert. When the credential is a delegation credential AND there is no cache, `CredentialActionsDropdown` returns null, but the wrapper still renders an empty 128px-wide box in the top-right of every calendar card. Either conditionally render the wrapper (`canDisconnect || hasCache`) or have `CredentialActionsDropdown` render an empty placeholder of the same size so the layout does not shift.

findings.title: deleteCache input is not constrained to positive integers
findings.body: The mutation uses `z.object({ credentialId: z.number() })`. `z.number()` accepts floats, negatives, NaN-passing types, and any integer range. For a database id, this should be `z.number().int().positive()` (or a dedicated `ZDeleteCacheInputSchema` similar to other inputs in this router) so the handler can't be invoked with nonsense values and so the type carries semantic meaning. As written, a negative or zero `credentialId` is silently rejected inside the handler with a generic `Credential not found or access denied`, masking bad input.

findings.title: Migration warning text contradicts the migration body
findings.body: The generated warning block says: `Added the required column "updatedAt" to the "CalendarCache" table without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty.` The actual migration below it adds the column with `DEFAULT NOW()`, so the warning is incorrect and would mislead a reviewer/operator who only reads the header. The comment should describe what the migration actually does (`Added the required column "updatedAt" with a default of NOW() to safely backfill existing rows.`).

findings.title: findMany loses type-level validation by dropping the `satisfies` clause
findings.body: The diff for `findMany` removes the `const args = { where, select, orderBy } satisfies Prisma.SelectedCalendarFindManyArgs;` line and inlines the call. The `satisfies` previously caught a class of type mismatches between the custom `FindManyArgs` type and the actual `Prisma.SelectedCalendarFindManyArgs` (for example an unknown orderBy key, or a where shape that Prisma doesn't support). Without it, callers like `watchCalendar` and `unwatchCalendar` that rely on `googleChannelId: { not: null }` and `orderBy: { userId: "asc" | "desc" }` are no longer type-checked at this boundary. Keep the `satisfies` (or the equivalent explicit type annotation) to preserve the previous type safety.

findings.title: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache bumps updatedAt for calendars that were just unwatched
findings.body: The new line `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` updates `updatedAt` for *every* SelectedCalendar of the credential, not just the `remainingCalendars` that the function was actually called with. In the `unwatchCalendar` path this means the calendars whose `googleChannelId` was just cleared (and that are no longer being watched) also get their `updatedAt` stamped to NOW(), which contradicts the intent expressed in the PR notes ("SelectedCalendar.updatedAt ... only updated via Google webhook handler"). Either restrict the update to the calendars passed in, or drop this side-effect entirely if it has no consumer.

findings.title: deleteCache handler accepts any credential the user owns, with no rate limit and no audit log
findings.body: The handler checks `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { id: credentialId, userId: user.id } })` and then unconditionally deletes all CalendarCache rows for that credential. Issues: (1) there is no rate limiting, so a malicious or buggy client can repeatedly force cache rebuilds for any of their own Google credentials (cost + latency). (2) The mutation deletes the cache for *all* users that share this credential - the check only verifies `userId === ctx.user.id`, but in team/org setups a single credential may back multiple users' bookings, and a single user wiping it affects the whole group. At minimum, log who triggered the wipe and the credential, and consider whether org/team members should also be allowed. (3) The `credentialId` in the where clause is the only scope; selecting only cache entries that belong to the requesting user (via `CalendarCache.userId`) would be safer where applicable.

findings.title: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds ignores expiresAt, so expired cache is reported as 'active'
findings.body: `getCachedAvailability` (and the cache hit path) deliberately filter by `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` so expired rows are treated as cache misses. `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` does not apply that filter and returns `_max.updatedAt` for the credential regardless of whether the latest row is expired. The UI therefore displays "Cache Status: Last updated ..." and exposes "Delete cached data" even when every cache row for the credential is already past `expiresAt` and will be ignored on the next read. Add the same `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` filter (or an equivalent `where: { expiresAt: { gt: new Date() } }`) so the cache status reflects what would actually be served.

findings.title: connectedCalendars now issues an extra DB round-trip on every render of the calendars settings
findings.body: The handler now always runs `cacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds(credentialIds)`, which executes a `prisma.calendarCache.groupBy` for every call to `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. That query is hit on every refetch (the wrapper sets `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`, but it still runs on mount, after `disconnectMutation.onSettled` invalidates it, and after onboarding). For users with many credentials this is an extra round-trip on the critical path of `/apps/installed/calendar`. Two cheap improvements: (a) only run it when there is at least one Google Calendar credential (the only consumer of `cacheUpdatedAt`), or (b) cache the result per-credentialId for a short TTL in `CalendarCacheRepository` since the value changes only when cache is written.

findings.title: No tests for deleteCache handler, getCacheStatusByCredentialIds, or the new UI component
findings.body: The PR introduces three new pieces of logic that each have security, data-integrity, or UX impact and none of them come with a test: (1) `deleteCache.handler.ts` performs an authz check and a destructive DB write - needs at least one test that a non-owner gets `Credential not found or access denied` and one that an owner succeeds and the cache rows are removed. (2) `CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` - needs a test that credentials with no cache rows are omitted and that `updatedAt` is the MAX across keys. (3) `CredentialActionsDropdown` - needs a test that the dropdown is hidden for non-Google credentials and for Google credentials without cache, and that "Delete cached data" is only available when `cacheUpdatedAt` is present. None of these test files appear in the diff.
